texts.preamble: State vs Chaggan Lal & Anr on 19 April, 2017 Author: Vijay Bishnoi Bench: Vijay Bishnoi High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At Jodhpur S.B. Crml Leave To Appeal No. 385 / 2015 State of Rajasthan ----Appellant Versus 1 . Chaggan Lal son of Ganga Ram by caste Arora resident of Binjhbayla Police Station Ghamudwali district Sri Ganganagar 2. Mukul Kishore son of Shri Radhey Shyam Berahmin resident of Rajpura district Patiyala, Punjab ----Respondent _____________________________________________________
texts.facts: Hence, the State has now preferred this leave to appeal before this Court. Learned Public Prosecutor has submitted that the delay in filing this leave to appeal is bonafide and, therefore, the same deserves to be condoned. State vs Chaggan Lal & Anr on 19 April, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86704250/ 1 After hearing learned counsels for the parties and after going through the averments made in the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, the same is allowed and the delay in filing this leave to appeal is condoned. Brief facts of the case are that PW.1 Raghunath Singh filed a complaint before the trial court on 01.04.2005 alleging therein that he was posted as Food Inspector in the Office of Chief Medical and Health Officer, Hanumangarh on 26.03.2004 and on that day at about 6:00 P.M., he inspected Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal situated at Dhan Mandi, Goluwala. At that time, Kundan Lal son of Ishardas Arora was present as the owner of the firm and was selling the food items. After introducing himself, he inspected the refined mustard oil (Bansri Brand) and on suspicion of adulteration, he purchased three one litre packets of said refined mustard oil and paid Rs.183/- to Kundanlal. The samples of said mustard oil were sent for chemical examination and from the report thereof, it was found that it was adulterated. A complaint for commission of offence under section 7/16 of the Act of 1954 was filed against the proprietor Kundanlal, Chhaganlal and Mukul Kishore, wherein, it was alleged that Kundanlal and Chhaganlal are the partners of Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal, whereas the accused-respondent Mukul Kishore was the nominee of the company, which had manufactured the said adulterated mustard oil. The trial court after taking cognizance against the accused-respondents had framed charges for the aforesaid offence against them. It is noticed that during the course of trial, one of the accused-respondent Kundanlal died and, therefore, the trial (4 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] against him was dropped. To prove its case, the prosecution had produced three witnesses and also got exhibited as many as 30 documents. The statements of the accused-respondents were recorded under section 313 CrPC and in defence, DW.1 Dr. Prem Kumar was produced. texts.arguments: Per contra, learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents Mr M.S.Singhvi assisted by Mr Angadh Mirdha & Mr Deepak Chandak has vehemently opposed the application seeking condonation of delay in filing this leave to appeal and argued that the State has failed to explain the delay in filing this leave to appeal sufficiently, hence, the delay is not liable to be condoned. Learned Public Prosecutor has submitted that the prosecution has sufficiently proved the fact that the accused- respondent Chhagan Lal was the partner of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal on the day when the inspection of the said firm was carried out by the Food Inspector PW.1 Raghunath Singh and samples of the adulterated mustard oil were collected. Learned Public Prosecutor has argued that PW.1 Raghunath Singh in his (5 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] statement before the court has specifically stated that accused- respondent Chhagan Lal was one of the partners of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal on 26.03.2004 and to substantiate the same, he also got exhibited a letter Ex.P/17 said to have been issued by the Assistant Commercial Taxation Officer, Hanumangarh dated 09.11.2004. It is contended that the trial court has not appreciated the said piece of evidence in right perspective. Learned Public Prosecutor has further argued that by producing Ex.P/18 and Ex.P/19 the prosecution has sufficiently proved that the accused-respondent Mukul Kishore was the nominee of the company on 26.03.2004, however, the trial court without appreciating the said piece of evidence has illegally held that the prosecution has failed to prove that on the day when the inspection was carried out by the Food Inspector in the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal, the accused-respondent Mukul Kishore was the authorized nominee of Amrit Enterprises, which had allegedly manufactured the adulterated mustard oil. Learned Public Prosecutor has, therefore, submitted that in view of the evidence produced by the prosecution before the trial court, prima facie it is proved that the trial court has grossly erred in acquitting the accused-respondents. Hence, it is a fit case wherein the leave should be granted. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents has argued that since the prosecution has failed to prove that the accused-respondent Chhagan Lal was the partner of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal on 26.03.2004, the trial court has rightly acquitted the accused-respondents from the offence punishable (6 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] under section 7/16 (1) a (i) of the Act of 1954. It is contended that respondent - Chhagan Lal was partner of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal from 31.05.1977 to 03.09.1995 and from 04.09.1995, the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal was a proprietorship firm to which late Kundan Lal was the sole proprietor. It is also contended that from Ex.P/6, From VI produced along with the complaint, it is clear that late Kundan Lal was the proprietor of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal. Learned counsel for the respondents has invited the attention of this Court towards Ex.D/1, a certificate issued by the Assistant Commercial Taxation Officer, Hanumangarh on 20.09.2005, wherein it is certified that Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal was a partnership firm from 31.05.1977 to State vs Chaggan Lal & Anr on 19 April, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86704250/ 3 03.09.1995 and thereafter the said firm became the proprietorship firm of which late Kundan Lal was the proprietor. Learned counsel for the respondent has, therefore, submitted that from the above fact, it is clear that on the day i.e. 26.03.2004 when the Food Inspector inspected the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal and collected samples of the refined mustard oil, the respondent Chhagan Lal was not the partner of the firm. Learned counsel for the respondents has further argued that the prosecution has failed to produce cogent and reliable evidence to prove that on 26.03.2004, respondent - Mukul Kishore was the authorized nominee of the Amrit Enterprises, who had allegedly manufactured the adulterated mustard oil. Learned counsel for the respondents has also argued that the prosecution has failed to prove that Ex.P/18 and Ex.P/19 were issued by the (7 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] authorized signatory of the Amrit Enterprises or the Local Health Authority of Abohar (Punjab), where the Amrit Enterprises is situated. It is contended that Ex.P/18 and Ex.P/19 have not been proved by the prosecution by producing any witness regarding the issuance of the said documents. Learned counsel for the respondents has, therefore, submitted that the trial court has rightly held that the prosecution has failed to prove that on the day i.e. 26.03.2004 when the Food Inspector inspected the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal at Goluwala and collected the samples of adulterated mustard oil, respondent- Mukul Kishore was the authorized nominee of the Amrit Enterprises, which had manufactured the said mustard oil. Learned counsel for the respondents has, therefore, prayed that in view of the above facts and circumstances of the case, no case for grant of leave is made out, hence, the leave to appeal to this Court is liable to be rejected.
